jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. stackOverflowQuestions.title: Go net.Conn.Close() hangs forever in poll.(*FD).Close (semacquire) with no goroutine using the socket

We've seen this three times in production, and only a restart fixes it. Environment: Go 1.26 , linux/arm64 (AWS Graviton), Aerospike Go client v7.10.2, plain TCP. The Aerospike client closes idle pooled connections while holding the pool's mutex. That Close() was stuck for 8+ minutes, so about 13,800 goroutines piled up behind the mutex: goroutine 25698717 [semacquire, 8 minutes]: internal/poll.runtime_Semacquire(...) internal/poll.(*FD).Close(0x3daa96edf800) internal/poll/fd_unix.go:114 net.(*conn).Close(...) net/net.go:220 github.com/aerospike/aerospike-client-go/v7.(*Connection).Close(...) github.com/aerospike/aerospike-client-go/v7.(*singleConnectionHeap).DropIdleTail(...) As we understand it, FD.Close waits until no other goroutine is using the descriptor. But in two dumps taken 54 seconds apart, no goroutine was in any Aerospike connection read, write or deadline call. Every other goroutine in internal/poll was on an unrelated socket (gRPC/HTTP connections and listeners). Questions What could keep the descriptor's reference count above zero with no goroutine using it? How can we inspect the fdMutex state, e.g. from a core dump with Delve?

quantaArticles.title: Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence?
quantaArticles.description: A mathematical mechanism enables AI models to process language at scale, undergirding the current AI revolution. Our columnist asks: Why is attention the key?
quantaArticles.author: Natalie Wolchover

quantaArticles.title: How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own.
quantaArticles.description: C.H. Waddington’s powerful image of embryonic stem cells specializing on a rolling landscape has captivated biologists since the 1950s. Experimental data is finally confirming, and complicating, his visionary ideas.
quantaArticles.author: Philip Ball

quantaArticles.title: As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
quantaArticles.description: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.
quantaArticles.author: Ben Brubaker

quantaArticles.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
quantaArticles.description: Mathematicians are facing the sudden shift with grief, anger, and a desperate search for fresh ideas: “If we don’t adapt, there’s just no more math in 50 years.”
quantaArticles.author: Jordana Cepelewicz

quantaArticles.title: Sea Monkeys Show Scientists How To Rewrite a Rule of Turbulence
quantaArticles.description: Scientists assumed that energy flows in only one direction in a turbulent system. What they didn’t know, until they looked closely at brine shrimp, was that a simple factor can reverse the flow.
quantaArticles.author: Stephen Ornes

infoqArticles.title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
infoqArticles.description: Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in recovery for Software Template tasks, resuming crashed or timed-out runs from the last completed step. The release also carries breaking changes to the catalog, search and TechDocs, so teams should review their configuration before upgrading to the current 1.55.3 patch. By Mark Silvester
infoqArticles.author: Mark Silvester

infoqArticles.title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
infoqArticles.description: A critical remote command execution vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570, poses risks by allowing unauthorized access to mailbox data and credentials. This flaw, stemming from improper input sanitization, has been actively exploited. Organizations are advised to upgrade to version 10.1.20 or disable susceptible SNMP services to mitigate risks. By Olimpiu Po
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
infoqArticles.description: Once AI is in production, code arrives faster than it can be reviewed, token costs rise, evals have to be good enough to act on, and agents need permissions and guardrails. QCon AI New York 2026 (December 15-16) has confirmed sessions from engineers sharing how they handle these constraints. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
infoqArticles.description: AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: How Eve Online Leverages Head Based Sampling to Observe "Fun"
infoqArticles.description: Nicholas Herring shares how EVE Online tackles distributed tracing and observability across a 20-year-old MMO architecture. He discusses leveraging head-based, dynamic exponential moving average (EMA), and deterministic sampling techniques to maintain high system fidelity, control telemetry costs, and avoid performance degradation under high-throughput real-time game simulations. By Nicholas Herri
infoqArticles.author: Nicholas Herring

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive Through Cloudflare
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests for an origin. The design choice drawing attention is a refusal: the Gateway will not decrypt requests arriving from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare, because that would put client identifiers and request contents in the same hands. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Spotify More Than Doubled Monthly Code Changes as AI Accelerated Development
infoqArticles.description: Spotify reports that AI-assisted development more than doubled monthly merged changes, prompting a review of quality and reliability controls across its engineering organization. The company describes changes to testing, observability, rollback capacity, workload prioritization, and automated maintenance as it adapts to higher software change volume. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Article: When Should You Use Liquid Clustering? Benchmarking Lakehouse Layout Strategies
infoqArticles.description: Physical data layout is one of the most consequential decisions in lakehouse engineering. The author compares Liquid Clustering, ZOrdering, and partitioning across four workload types on Delta Lake, uncovering two undocumented failure modes that likely affect production systems today and offering a decision framework for choosing the right layout strategy. By Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma
infoqArticles.author: Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma

infoqArticles.title: Podcast: What Does It Really Mean To Program With AI: A Conversation with Joy Ebertz
infoqArticles.description: In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Joy Ebertz about how the use of artificial intelligence is changing the way architects and developers do their jobs. Focusing on the long term success of the business is one of the most neglected tasks of an architect. This task becomes particularly important as the nature of artificial intelligence changes the landscape of software development. By Joy Ebe
infoqArticles.author: Joy Ebertz

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
infoqArticles.description: Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028. By Erik Peterson
infoqArticles.author: Erik Peterson

infoqArticles.title: React 19.3: Adds a browser() API, Giving Client-Only Rendering a First-Class Name
infoqArticles.description: React 19.3 was released on September 9, introducing several features including the react-dom browser() API. This API allows components to opt out of server-side rendering, addressing issues with components that rely on client-specific data. It provides a cleaner solution for managing hydration mismatches and supports conditional data fetching, enhancing flexibility for developers. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Java News Roundup: Grails 8, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Infinispan, LangChain4j, Spock
infoqArticles.description: This week's Java roundup for October 5th, 2026, features news highlighting: OpenJDK JEPs Proposed to Target for JDK 28; Lazy Constants elevated to Candidate status; the GA releases of Apache Grails 8.0 and Open Liberty 20.0.0.10; point releases of TornadoVM, Infinispan, LangChain4j and Spock; and a maintenance release of GlassFish. By Michael Redlich
infoqArticles.author: Michael Redlich

infoqArticles.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
infoqArticles.description: GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending. By Matt Saunders
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: Xcode 27.2 Introduces an Agent- and Merge-Friendly JSON Format for Project Configuration
infoqArticles.description: Apple is introducing a new JSON-based format for Xcode project configuration files, replacing the traditional property-list-based format. Available in Xcode 27.2, the new format aims to improve readability, simplify maintenance, and make project configuration easier for AI coding agents to understand and modify. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
infoqArticles.description: Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone
